items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I worked in another big band in Washington -- was the Hardy Brothers.

ctx.x: -- and another house band I worked with steady there -- I worked in another big band in Washington -- was the Hardy Brothers. That was -- now, that was a good show band. They could -- on the stage they knew how to throw their horns up and down. They did the same routines like Lunceford did, but only this is way before Lunceford. They were doing these kinds of routines way back there then.
What were the Hardy Brothers first names?

Wesley Hardy was one, and I can't think of the other guy's name. Wesley was the thin one, then there's a fat one we called Horse. I never did know Horse's name. But these were the two Hardy Brothers. But they weren't the leaders of the band. The leader of the band was Coleridge Davis, piano player. He led the band and did the arrangements.
